Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 65-year-old man with sudden inability to move left arm, left facial tingling, dysphagia, and speech difficulty; emergency ambulance arranged for suspected acute stroke.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Awoke ~1 hour ago unable to move left arm; no pain. Left facial tingling started simultaneously.
- Associated symptoms: Mild difficulty swallowing; speech feels slower/harder. No left-leg symptoms, no hand discoloration, no coldness.
- Pertinent negatives: No prior similar episodes.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Losartan (dose/route/frequency not documented); Amlodipine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Penicillin (reaction not specified).
- Family history: Father with heart disease.
- Social: Lives alone. Former smoker. Alcohol: several pints of beer on weekends plus a couple during the week. No other social factors noted.

Examination:
- (Telephone consultation – no physical examination or vitals obtained.)

Impression:
- Suspected acute cerebrovascular accident (stroke) with unilateral arm weakness, facial paresthesia, dysphagia, and dysarthria.

Plan:
- GP arranged emergency ambulance to patient’s home for immediate transfer to nearest emergency department/stroke unit.
- Advised patient to unlock front door and wait in hallway for paramedics.
- Clinician remained on the line until ambulance arrival.
- Hospital team to assess for eligibility for acute stroke therapies (e.g., thrombolysis) per protocol.

Quality checks:

● Missing clinically expected elements: Vital signs, objective neurological examination, blood glucose check, full medication doses/routes/frequencies, comprehensive allergy details, surgical history, current smoking status details.
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
● Transcript quality: Clear audible transcript; telephone format limits examination data.
